source_documents.title: Rational Design of Red AIEgens with New Core Structure from Non-Emissive Heteroaromatics

reference_evidence_units.quote: TAA-4PTPA exhibited faint but much redder emission at ca. 708 nm in THF.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TAA-4PTPA

reference_evidence_units.quote: whereas, in TAA-4PTPA, CT transition became dominant.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TAA-4PTPA

reference_evidence_units.quote: TAA-4PTPA allowed it to relax to twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT) state easily by molecular motion upon excitation
reference_evidence_units.subject: TAA-4PTPA

reference_evidence_units.quote: However, in the solid, the motion of TAA-4PTPA was better restricted.
reference_evidence_units.subject: TAA-4PTPA
reference_evidence_units.statement: Restricted motion in the solid (Φ 8.0% vs 1%).

reference_evidence_units.quote: attaching TAA with phenyl rotors can change the transition component from n→π* transition to π→π* transition, thus increasing the irradiative transition component of TAA derivative
reference_evidence_units.subject: TAA derivatives
reference_evidence_units.statement: Phenyl rotors switch the S1 from nπ* to ππ*, raising radiative character.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Phenyl/amine rotor motion drives nonradiative relaxation in solution and is restricted in the solid.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Donor-decorated TAA core forms a CT-dominated state that relaxes to TICT in solution.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Rates quantify the weak solution emission; the core design switches nπ* to ππ* to gain radiative character.
